page: Amazon Web Services x8i.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores with hyper-threading operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in memory-intensive and computational tasks. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core execution, image processing, and text processing, alongside strong performance in multi-core Geekbench, software compilation, and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is strong, though large-block uncached read and write operations fall into the average tier. The processor support for Advanced Matrix Extensions and Advanced Vector Extensions contributes to top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds for small language models, as well as strong prompt processing for larger 7B and 70B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the x8i.12xlarge offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, leveraging DDR5 speeds to optimize memory-heavy operations without the overhead of local storage. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy applications. This instance is highly suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
